latestRelease.title: v1.40.1
latestRelease.notes:
## This is a patch release.

### What's Changed

- Fixed connection-state handling in squashed pipelines. Commands following `AUTH`, `SELECT`, `HELLO`, `CLIENT`, or `RESET` now observe the updated connection state instead of stale authentication, database, or RESP protocol state ([#8016](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/pull/8016)).
- Fixed compressed QList node memory accounting and defragmentation ([#8011](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/pull/8011), [#8014](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/pull/8014)).

Full Changelog: [v1.40.0...v1.40.1](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/compare/v1.40.0...v1.40.1)
highlights: Fixed connection-state handling in squashed pipelines. Commands following AUTH, SELECT, HELLO, CLIENT, or RESET now observe the updated connection state instead of stale authentication, database, or RESP protocol state (#8016).
Fixed compressed QList node memory accounting and defragmentation (#8011, #8014).

signals.title: Tiering: Small bins don't account for key size
signals.text: Currently, we determine whether a entry should be offloaded based just on its value length. When we serialize a small bin page, we also write the _key_ to be able to trace the value back for defragmentation (and +2 bytes dbid). However, _we never check the size of the key_. This first leads to the fact that we can have underutilized pages, as key+value can be more than 50%. Second, having a long key with a value eligible for small bins will just write over the buffer and corrupt everything -> there are no safeguards for key lenghts What makes this not starightforwards to fix, is that in all our codebase we deduce the category (small, standalone) based only on the value size. Values with long keys should either produce undefragmentable pages (by not storing the key) or be offloaded on their own Will fix #8024, #8012
signals.author: dranikpg

signals.title: crash: main_service.cc:1669] Check failed: rb->RepliesRecorded() > replies_recorded_ (0 vs. 0) CF.ADD
signals.text:
Found by analysing the AFL++ RESP fuzz run [31959833026](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/actions/runs/31959833026) - 14 of its 20 crash artifacts are this bug. Reproduction (the 4 GiB cap is required): ```bash mkdir -p /tmp/dfA/db ( ulimit -v 4194304; exec ./build-dbg/dragonfly --port=7793 --proactor_threads=1 \ --dbfilename= --dir=/tmp/dfA/db --alsologtostderr ) & redis-cli -p 7793 CF.RESERVE cf 1000 BUCKETSIZE 4 MAXITERATIONS 100 EXPANSION 2 for i in $(seq 1 200); do printf 'MULTI
CF.ADD cf item1
EXEC
'; done | redis-cli -p 7793 ``` Aborts on the 153rd iteration, 5/5 runs: ``` E main_service.cc:1717] Internal error, system probably unstable std::bad_alloc F main_service.cc:1669] Check failed: rb->RepliesRecorded() > replies_recorded_ (0 vs. 0) CF.ADD N6facade21CapturingReplyBuilderE ``` Two defects: 1. **Cuckoo filter growth is bounded by sub-filter count, not by memory.** Because an item's two candidate buckets form a 2-cycle, repeated adds of the same item can never be placed, and each expansion appends a sub-filter twice the size of the last. With `EXPANSION 2` a couple hundred adds reach a 512 MiB allocation, which throws. The expansion itself is not the defect. `CF.ADD` counts every add as a separate entry, and repeated items are documented to fill the filter up and expand it ([cuckoo filter docs](https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/probabilistic/cuckoo-filter/): "Adding the same element multiple times will create multiple entries, thus filling up your filter"). Upstream bounds growth by a count as well and carries the same exposure — what differs here is that the allocation failure is fatal. A fix has to keep expanding on duplicates and add a memory ceiling, not refuse duplicates. 2. **An exception has no handler on the squashed-`MULTI` path.** The squashed-stub callback has no try/catch, unlike the ordinary transaction callback, so the `bad_alloc` escapes into command dispatch, which logs it and returns without writing a reply — and the reply guard trips. Defect 2 is command-agnostic: any handler that throws inside `EXEC` hits it. In release builds the reply guard is compiled out and the command sends nothing at all. `EXEC` has already written its array header by then, so the client is left mid-array and consumes the next command's reply as the missing element — a connection desync, not just a short array. Note: do not simply copy the ordinary transaction callback's handlers into the squashed-stub path. It also has `catch (std::exception&) { LOG(FATAL) }`, which would turn today's silent no-reply into a hard release-build crash.
signals.author: vyavdoshenko

signals.title: crash: main_service.cc:2241] Script <sha> not found in script mgr — SCRIPT FLAGS on an unknown sha then EVALSHA
signals.text: Found by analysing the AFL++ RESP fuzz run [31959833026](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/actions/runs/31959833026) — 6 of its 20 crash artifacts are this bug. Reproduction — two commands, stock server, no special flags: ```bash ./build-dbg/dragonfly --port=7791 --dbfilename= --alsologtostderr & redis-cli -p 7791 SCRIPT FLAGS 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 no-writes redis-cli -p 7791 EVALSHA 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 0 ``` First returns `+OK`, second kills the server (`exit -6`), 5/5 runs: ``` F main_service.cc:2241] Script 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 not found in script mgr ``` Any 40-hex sha that was never loaded works. `ScriptMgr::ConfigCmd` does `auto& data = db_[key];` (`src/server/script_mgr.cc:181`) — an unconditional default-insert — then publishes the params to every thread. That leaves a sha whose *params* exist but whose *body* is `nullptr`. `EvalInternal`'s NOSCRIPT guard reads the params cache (`src/server/main_service.cc:2316-2319`) and passes, while `LoadScript` reads the body registry, which requires a non-null body (`src/server/script_mgr.cc:353`) and fails — hitting the `LOG(DFATAL)` at `src/server/main_service.cc:2241`. In release builds `DFATAL` is non-fatal, but execution then reaches `CHECK(result == Interpreter::RUN_OK)` at `src/server/main_service.cc:2464` — still `SIGABRT`.
signals.author: vyavdoshenko

signals.title: BF.LOADCHUNK of a header-only chunk produces an unloadable snapshot (data loss on restart) and aborts on COPY at generic_family.cc:435
signals.text: Found by analysing the AFL++ RESP fuzz run [31957444982](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/actions/runs/31957444982). The fuzzer found the `COPY` abort; the snapshot corruption below is the more severe consequence of the same defect. The 12-byte blob is a valid `BF.SCANDUMP` cursor-1 header (`uint32le version=1` + `double-le grow_factor=2.0`). **A — data loss, silent:** ```bash mkdir -p /tmp/dfC/db ./build-dbg/dragonfly --port=7788 --proactor_threads=1 --dbfilename=dump --dir=/tmp/dfC/db & redis-cli -p 7788 SET k1 v1 redis-cli -p 7788 BF.LOADCHUNK bkey 1 $'\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x40' # +OK redis-cli -p 7788 SAVE # +OK redis-cli -p 7788 SHUTDOWN ./build-dbg/dragonfly --port=7788 --proactor_threads=1 --dbfilename=dump --dir=/tmp/dfC/db ``` The restart exits 1 and every key in the snapshot is lost: ``` E rdb_load.cc:2673] Error while calling LoadKeyValPair(type, &settings): Internal error when loading RDB file 5 E server_family.cc:1541] Rdb load failed: Internal error when loading RDB file 5 ``` **B — abort, 5/5 runs:** ```bash redis-cli -p 7788 BF.LOADCHUNK bkey 1 $'\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x40' redis-cli -p 7788 COPY bkey dst ``` ``` E generic_family.cc:205] failed to load data for type id 34 F generic_family.cc:435] Error during rename command, deserialize_status: 5 del_status: 0 ``` `LoadSBFHeader` creates an SBF with zero filters and `fp_prob_ = 0.0` (`src/core/bloom.cc:410`). Query commands are guarded by `IsBeingLoaded()` (`src/server/bloom_family.cc:45-47`), but the serialization path is not: `SaveSBFObject` writes `fp_prob = 0.0` unvalidated (`src/server/rdb_save.cc:677-716`) and the loader rejects its own output, accepting only `(0, 0.5]` (`src/server/rdb_load.cc:2007`). `COPY` always takes the `Renamer` DUMP→RESTORE path (`src/server/generic_family.cc:2514`), unlike `RENAME`, which has a single-shard fast path. The same writer/loader asymmetry exists for fully-formed filters: `AddNewFilterToSBF` accepts `fp_prob` in `(0, 1)` (`src/core/bloom.cc:430`) while the loader accepts `(0, 0.5]`. Boundary verified: 0.50 survives, 0.51 aborts. A fix should close the range mismatch, not just the zero-filter case. `BF.LOADCHUNK` is not a restricted command.
signals.author: vyavdoshenko

signals.title: ci(tests): add scheduled e2e workflow for ioredis client
signals.text: ## What Adds a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow, `.github/workflows/ioredis-tests.yml`, that runs the existing [ioredis](https://github.com/luin/ioredis) end-to-end test suite against a freshly built Dragonfly binary every day, and points to it from `tests/README.md`. ## Why (closes part of #383) `#383` asked for e2e coverage of the `ioredis` client. Looking at the history: - `tests/integration/ioredis.Dockerfile` and `tests/integration/run_ioredis_on_docker.sh` (added in #394 / #459) already give a local script + README instructions for running the curated ioredis test suite against Dragonfly (deliverables 1 & 2 from the issue). - What was still missing is what @romange asked for in the issue thread: *"we just need to run them via the testing pipeline on github"*. There was no CI workflow exercising these tests — `ioredis`/`node-redis`/`jedis` Dockerfiles are all local-only, and grepping every workflow in `.github/workflows` shows none of them touch `tests/integration`. - The repo already has exactly this pattern for another ioredis-based client, `bullmq-tests.yml` (nightly scheduled job, builds Dragonfly from source, installs Node, runs the client's own test suite with a skip-list). This PR mirrors that same structure for `ioredis` itself, reusing the pre-existing `tests/integration/.run_ioredis_valid_test.sh` skip/grep list rather than duplicating it. ## What this does NOT do - It does not touch the existing local Docker scripts — those keep working as-is for local development. - It does not attempt the issue's "bonus" deliverable (a bespoke Dragonfly-authored pub/sub regression test); that's a separate, larger piece of work and is left as a possible follow-up so this PR stays focused on the CI-wiring gap. ## Testing Since building the full C++ project wasn't practical in my environment, I validated the actual test-execution path the workflow runs: - Started the official `dragonfly` Docker image (`--cluster_mode=emulated --lock_on_hashtags --dbfilename=`, same flags as `bullmq-tests.yml` uses for Dragonfly). - Cloned `luin/ioredis`, ran `npm install`, then ran the exact command the new workflow runs: `npm run env -- TS_NODE_TRANSPILE_ONLY=true NODE_ENV=test ./run_tests.sh` using the repo's own `tests/integration/.run_ioredis_valid_test.sh` as `run_tests.sh`. - Result: **493 passing / 2 failing**, both failures being `Timeout of 8000ms exceeded` on tests unrelated to correctness (a large-pipeline timing test and a cluster startup-nodes teardown hook) — consistent with the constrained local sandbox rather than a real regression. I couldn't run the pre-commit C++/format hooks in this environment (no C++ toolchain available), but this PR only touches a workflow YAML file and a doc file, so `clang-format`/`black` are not applicable. Closes (partially) #383
signals.author: vjymisal0

signals.title: server: Fix stream size memory accounting
signals.text: It has been seen in certain cases that the stream size accounting breaks due to a negative delta. In that case, the metrics depending on this type go completely wrong and start showing object size in terrabytes instead of a few GiB. There are a couple of fixes and safeguards: * original check that size>=delta if delta<0 was not doing anythingi it was always true. it is removed * now the change requested in bytes is compared with the curr. size and the limit ie 56 bit int maximum * if the value does not fit, then we do slow recomputation of the real size instead of clamping to 0 etc. There is also removed a buggy cast, previously we did something like: `SetSize(Size() + size)` So first the sum was cast to uint64_t, which might already wrap a negative value (if size is negative of more magnitude than Size()). Then that value was stored from uint64_t into a 56 bit field. In addition a negative delta was first cast by C++ itself to uint64_t. In the current code the cast for negative delta is done correctly and the case where delta is at boundary INT64_MIN is also handled --- The added test was failing without the changes.
signals.author: abhijat

signals.title: fix(pubsub): preserve V2 message ordering
signals.text: This PR fixes a known issue that was already fixed for V1 at 5ef35182. Defer V2 pipeline execution when queued control work predates the next parsed command. Let IoLoopV2 drain that work so UNSUBSCRIBE cannot discard earlier Pub/Sub messages. Tests: Extend the unsubscribe regression across V1 and V2 with standalone and deferred-GET commands. Bound the starvation publisher wave to assert fairness without treating ordered backlog as starvation.

signals.text: ## Summary - Lower the default `table_growth_margin` from `0.4` to `0.15`. - Reduce the conservative free-capacity estimate before allowing table growth. ## Test plan - `git diff --check` passed. - `ninja -C build-dbg dragonfly` reached and compiled `src/server/db_slice.cc`; the full build was blocked by the host filesystem running out of space.

signals.title: fix(tiering): tight small bin fragmentation cutoff
signals.text: For small bins, the smallest possible utilization for flushing a page is ~49% (because value + constant size header). We don't want this page to be considered for defragmentation (as it will livelock) so we pick a cutoff that is slightly lower (see the math on the PR). Also StashInfo.bytes `undercounted` because it never `included` the bytes wasted by each entry's header. Fix it by including the header entry overhead per value. Addresses properly both #8029 and #8024 and #8012
signals.author: kostasrim

signals.title: test: un-skip graceful shutdown test by asserting the guaranteed durability contract
signals.text: `test_gracefull_shutdown` (skipped since #1530) asserted strict equality between the last acknowledged INCR value and the snapshot content - a reply-before-close guarantee the server does not provide: shutdown drains in-flight commands for at most 10ms (best effort) and, at the TCP level, closing with unread request bytes triggers RST, so reply delivery cannot be guaranteed to a busy client at all. The invariant that *does* hold (snapshot is saved strictly after all connection fibers exit) is one-directional: every acknowledged write is in the snapshot, and at most one unacknowledged in-flight command per connection may exceed it. The test now asserts exactly that contract, deterministically. Changes: - Un-skip and rename to `TestGracefulShutdown::test_shutdown_snapshot_contains_acknowledged_writes` - Assert `acknowledged <= restored <= acknowledged + 1` per key, plus an explicit missing-key check - Dedicated control connection for SHUTDOWN; one pinned connection per worker with client retries disabled (the client library retries by default, and a silent re-send after a lost reply would corrupt acknowledgment accounting) - All SETs acknowledged before the increment loops start, so every key must exist after restart - `df_server.wait()` before restarting (snapshot fully written, no port race) and `wait_available_async()` after (avoid the loading phase) - Dynamic port instead of hardcoded 1111 Addresses the `test_gracefull_shutdown` item in #8028.
signals.author: vyavdoshenko

signals.title: feat(server): make conn_use_incoming_cpu runtime mutable
signals.text: ## Summary `conn_use_incoming_cpu` controls how new connections are distributed across proactor threads, and `Listener::PickConnectionProactor` already reads it on every accept — but it is not registered in the config registry, so changing it requires a restart. This PR registers it as mutable, so `CONFIG SET conn_use_incoming_cpu <bool>` takes effect immediately for new connections. No behavior change unless CONFIG SET is used. ## Motivation The flag's own comment notes it is only safe with correct RPS tuning: *"connections will be handled only on the CPUs that handle the softirqs for the incoming packets. To avoid imbalance in CPU load, RPS tuning is strongly advised."* In practice, steering misconfiguration is discovered in production. On one of our deployments (144 vCPUs; NIC IRQs pinned to CPUs 0–15, Dragonfly on 16–143) an RPS mask covering only part of the worker range concentrated **all** connections on 47 of 128 threads. A latency blip then became a self-feeding reconnect storm: the overloaded connection threads slowed replies, clients timed out and reconnected, and every new connection landed on the same hot threads. The only remedies were adding a replica or restarting the loaded master. With the flag mutable, an operator can flip placement to round-robin at runtime to break such a loop (optionally recycling clients gradually with `CLIENT KILL`), and flip it back once steering is fixed — no restart needed. ## Why changing it at runtime is safe - The flag is read exactly once per accept via `absl::GetFlag` (thread-safe), and the decision is consumed immediately. No state is derived from or cached based on the flag anywhere else: `ProactorPool::MapCpuToThreads` is built once at pool startup and is only consulted, never mutated, by the placement path. - A toggle only affects **future** accepts. Existing connections are placed once at accept time and are never re-placed, so they cannot be affected by a change. - An accept racing a `CONFIG SET` observes either the old or the new value — both select a well-defined placement path, and the incoming-cpu path already degrades gracefully to round-robin when the reported CPU has no matching thread. The added test exercises exactly this: 4 workers churn 80 fresh connections (each doing SET/GET) **concurrently with 40 flag flips**, while 5 connections established before any toggle hold state throughout — all operations succeed and the pre-existing connections remain intact and correct afterwards. ## Changes - Register `conn_use_incoming_cpu` as mutable in the config registry. - Add `test_conn_use_incoming_cpu`: `CONFIG GET`/`SET` round-trip, new-connection creation raced against concurrent toggles, and verification that connections predating the toggles are unaffected. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
signals.author: shahyash2609

signals.title: fix(facade): log V2 traffic before dispatch
signals.text: Move V2 traffic logging out of ParseRedis: V2 can call it from a receive callback that must not preempt, while logging may suspend. Log at the pre-dispatch boundary instead, preserving squashing and dispatch order. V1 stays the same. Extend DispatchSquashedBatch with an optional pre-dispatch callback that is invoked for each accepted command immediately before execution. has_unparsed_input preserves parser-buffer continuation metadata when logging is deferred. Tests cover ordered V1/V2 pipeline records and V2 proactor parsing without preemption.
signals.author: glevkovich

signals.title: fix: null reply shapes for blocking moves, LPOP COUNT, ZRANK WITHSCORE, EXEC and friends
signals.text: Follow-up to #8092: fixes the remaining commands whose null replies use the wrong RESP2 kind (null bulk string vs null array), plus two reverse cases where a null array was sent where a scalar null belongs. Changes: - BRPOPLPUSH/BLMOVE: a blocked timeout now replies a null array; inside MULTI/scripts (blocking denied) the reply stays a scalar null. - LPOP/RPOP with COUNT and ZRANK/ZREVRANK with WITHSCORE reply a null array on a missing key/member; without the option the scalar null is unchanged. - EXEC aborted by a WATCH (modified or expired key) replies a null array. - GEOPOS: missing members (and a missing key) produce null-array elements. - XPENDING summary with an empty PEL: the consumers element is a null array; min/max ids stay scalar nulls. - XINFO STREAM: empty `first-entry`/`last-entry` are scalar nulls, not null arrays (wrong in both RESP2 and RESP3 before). - COMMAND INFO: an unknown command name gets a null entry inside the reply array instead of a bare null. - Tests: existing assertions updated in place; added BLMOVE-under-MULTI and EXEC-abort-by-expiry coverage (the latter path was previously unreached by the suite). Part of the null-reply cleanup started in #8087 / #8092.

signal.title: crash: main_service.cc:1669] Check failed: rb->RepliesRecorded() > replies_recorded_ (0 vs. 0) CF.ADD
signal.text:
Found by analysing the AFL++ RESP fuzz run [31959833026](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/actions/runs/31959833026) - 14 of its 20 crash artifacts are this bug. Reproduction (the 4 GiB cap is required): ```bash mkdir -p /tmp/dfA/db ( ulimit -v 4194304; exec ./build-dbg/dragonfly --port=7793 --proactor_threads=1 \ --dbfilename= --dir=/tmp/dfA/db --alsologtostderr ) & redis-cli -p 7793 CF.RESERVE cf 1000 BUCKETSIZE 4 MAXITERATIONS 100 EXPANSION 2 for i in $(seq 1 200); do printf 'MULTI
CF.ADD cf item1
EXEC
'; done | redis-cli -p 7793 ``` Aborts on the 153rd iteration, 5/5 runs: ``` E main_service.cc:1717] Internal error, system probably unstable std::bad_alloc F main_service.cc:1669] Check failed: rb->RepliesRecorded() > replies_recorded_ (0 vs. 0) CF.ADD N6facade21CapturingReplyBuilderE ``` Two defects: 1. **Cuckoo filter growth is bounded by sub-filter count, not by memory.** Because an item's two candidate buckets form a 2-cycle, repeated adds of the same item can never be placed, and each expansion appends a sub-filter twice the size of the last. With `EXPANSION 2` a couple hundred adds reach a 512 MiB allocation, which throws. The expansion itself is not the defect. `CF.ADD` counts every add as a separate entry, and repeated items are documented to fill the filter up and expand it ([cuckoo filter docs](https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/data-types/probabilistic/cuckoo-filter/): "Adding the same element multiple times will create multiple entries, thus filling up your filter"). Upstream bounds growth by a count as well and carries the same exposure — what differs here is that the allocation failure is fatal. A fix has to keep expanding on duplicates and add a memory ceiling, not refuse duplicates. 2. **An exception has no handler on the squashed-`MULTI` path.** The squashed-stub callback has no try/catch, unlike the ordinary transaction callback, so the `bad_alloc` escapes into command dispatch, which logs it and returns without writing a reply — and the reply guard trips. Defect 2 is command-agnostic: any handler that throws inside `EXEC` hits it. In release builds the reply guard is compiled out and the command sends nothing at all. `EXEC` has already written its array header by then, so the client is left mid-array and consumes the next command's reply as the missing element — a connection desync, not just a short array. Note: do not simply copy the ordinary transaction callback's handlers into the squashed-stub path. It also has `catch (std::exception&) { LOG(FATAL) }`, which would turn today's silent no-reply into a hard release-build crash.

signal.title: fix(tiering): tight small bin fragmentation cutoff
signal.text: For small bins, the smallest possible utilization for flushing a page is ~49% (because value + constant size header). We don't want this page to be considered for defragmentation (as it will livelock) so we pick a cutoff that is slightly lower (see the math on the PR). Also StashInfo.bytes `undercounted` because it never `included` the bytes wasted by each entry's header. Fix it by including the header entry overhead per value. Addresses properly both #8029 and #8024 and #8012
signal.author: kostasrim

signal.title: Tiering: Small bins don't account for key size
signal.text: Currently, we determine whether a entry should be offloaded based just on its value length. When we serialize a small bin page, we also write the _key_ to be able to trace the value back for defragmentation (and +2 bytes dbid). However, _we never check the size of the key_. This first leads to the fact that we can have underutilized pages, as key+value can be more than 50%. Second, having a long key with a value eligible for small bins will just write over the buffer and corrupt everything -> there are no safeguards for key lenghts What makes this not starightforwards to fix, is that in all our codebase we deduce the category (small, standalone) based only on the value size. Values with long keys should either produce undefragmentable pages (by not storing the key) or be offloaded on their own Will fix #8024, #8012
signal.author: dranikpg

signal.title: BF.LOADCHUNK of a header-only chunk produces an unloadable snapshot (data loss on restart) and aborts on COPY at generic_family.cc:435
signal.text: Found by analysing the AFL++ RESP fuzz run [31957444982](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/actions/runs/31957444982). The fuzzer found the `COPY` abort; the snapshot corruption below is the more severe consequence of the same defect. The 12-byte blob is a valid `BF.SCANDUMP` cursor-1 header (`uint32le version=1` + `double-le grow_factor=2.0`). **A — data loss, silent:** ```bash mkdir -p /tmp/dfC/db ./build-dbg/dragonfly --port=7788 --proactor_threads=1 --dbfilename=dump --dir=/tmp/dfC/db & redis-cli -p 7788 SET k1 v1 redis-cli -p 7788 BF.LOADCHUNK bkey 1 $'\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x40' # +OK redis-cli -p 7788 SAVE # +OK redis-cli -p 7788 SHUTDOWN ./build-dbg/dragonfly --port=7788 --proactor_threads=1 --dbfilename=dump --dir=/tmp/dfC/db ``` The restart exits 1 and every key in the snapshot is lost: ``` E rdb_load.cc:2673] Error while calling LoadKeyValPair(type, &settings): Internal error when loading RDB file 5 E server_family.cc:1541] Rdb load failed: Internal error when loading RDB file 5 ``` **B — abort, 5/5 runs:** ```bash redis-cli -p 7788 BF.LOADCHUNK bkey 1 $'\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x40' redis-cli -p 7788 COPY bkey dst ``` ``` E generic_family.cc:205] failed to load data for type id 34 F generic_family.cc:435] Error during rename command, deserialize_status: 5 del_status: 0 ``` `LoadSBFHeader` creates an SBF with zero filters and `fp_prob_ = 0.0` (`src/core/bloom.cc:410`). Query commands are guarded by `IsBeingLoaded()` (`src/server/bloom_family.cc:45-47`), but the serialization path is not: `SaveSBFObject` writes `fp_prob = 0.0` unvalidated (`src/server/rdb_save.cc:677-716`) and the loader rejects its own output, accepting only `(0, 0.5]` (`src/server/rdb_load.cc:2007`). `COPY` always takes the `Renamer` DUMP→RESTORE path (`src/server/generic_family.cc:2514`), unlike `RENAME`, which has a single-shard fast path. The same writer/loader asymmetry exists for fully-formed filters: `AddNewFilterToSBF` accepts `fp_prob` in `(0, 1)` (`src/core/bloom.cc:430`) while the loader accepts `(0, 0.5]`. Boundary verified: 0.50 survives, 0.51 aborts. A fix should close the range mismatch, not just the zero-filter case. `BF.LOADCHUNK` is not a restricted command.
signal.author: vyavdoshenko

signal.title: crash: main_service.cc:2241] Script <sha> not found in script mgr — SCRIPT FLAGS on an unknown sha then EVALSHA
signal.text: Found by analysing the AFL++ RESP fuzz run [31959833026](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/actions/runs/31959833026) — 6 of its 20 crash artifacts are this bug. Reproduction — two commands, stock server, no special flags: ```bash ./build-dbg/dragonfly --port=7791 --dbfilename= --alsologtostderr & redis-cli -p 7791 SCRIPT FLAGS 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 no-writes redis-cli -p 7791 EVALSHA 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 0 ``` First returns `+OK`, second kills the server (`exit -6`), 5/5 runs: ``` F main_service.cc:2241] Script 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 not found in script mgr ``` Any 40-hex sha that was never loaded works. `ScriptMgr::ConfigCmd` does `auto& data = db_[key];` (`src/server/script_mgr.cc:181`) — an unconditional default-insert — then publishes the params to every thread. That leaves a sha whose *params* exist but whose *body* is `nullptr`. `EvalInternal`'s NOSCRIPT guard reads the params cache (`src/server/main_service.cc:2316-2319`) and passes, while `LoadScript` reads the body registry, which requires a non-null body (`src/server/script_mgr.cc:353`) and fails — hitting the `LOG(DFATAL)` at `src/server/main_service.cc:2241`. In release builds `DFATAL` is non-fatal, but execution then reaches `CHECK(result == Interpreter::RUN_OK)` at `src/server/main_service.cc:2464` — still `SIGABRT`.
signal.author: vyavdoshenko

signal.title: ci(tests): add scheduled e2e workflow for ioredis client
signal.text: ## What Adds a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow, `.github/workflows/ioredis-tests.yml`, that runs the existing [ioredis](https://github.com/luin/ioredis) end-to-end test suite against a freshly built Dragonfly binary every day, and points to it from `tests/README.md`. ## Why (closes part of #383) `#383` asked for e2e coverage of the `ioredis` client. Looking at the history: - `tests/integration/ioredis.Dockerfile` and `tests/integration/run_ioredis_on_docker.sh` (added in #394 / #459) already give a local script + README instructions for running the curated ioredis test suite against Dragonfly (deliverables 1 & 2 from the issue). - What was still missing is what @romange asked for in the issue thread: *"we just need to run them via the testing pipeline on github"*. There was no CI workflow exercising these tests — `ioredis`/`node-redis`/`jedis` Dockerfiles are all local-only, and grepping every workflow in `.github/workflows` shows none of them touch `tests/integration`. - The repo already has exactly this pattern for another ioredis-based client, `bullmq-tests.yml` (nightly scheduled job, builds Dragonfly from source, installs Node, runs the client's own test suite with a skip-list). This PR mirrors that same structure for `ioredis` itself, reusing the pre-existing `tests/integration/.run_ioredis_valid_test.sh` skip/grep list rather than duplicating it. ## What this does NOT do - It does not touch the existing local Docker scripts — those keep working as-is for local development. - It does not attempt the issue's "bonus" deliverable (a bespoke Dragonfly-authored pub/sub regression test); that's a separate, larger piece of work and is left as a possible follow-up so this PR stays focused on the CI-wiring gap. ## Testing Since building the full C++ project wasn't practical in my environment, I validated the actual test-execution path the workflow runs: - Started the official `dragonfly` Docker image (`--cluster_mode=emulated --lock_on_hashtags --dbfilename=`, same flags as `bullmq-tests.yml` uses for Dragonfly). - Cloned `luin/ioredis`, ran `npm install`, then ran the exact command the new workflow runs: `npm run env -- TS_NODE_TRANSPILE_ONLY=true NODE_ENV=test ./run_tests.sh` using the repo's own `tests/integration/.run_ioredis_valid_test.sh` as `run_tests.sh`. - Result: **493 passing / 2 failing**, both failures being `Timeout of 8000ms exceeded` on tests unrelated to correctness (a large-pipeline timing test and a cluster startup-nodes teardown hook) — consistent with the constrained local sandbox rather than a real regression. I couldn't run the pre-commit C++/format hooks in this environment (no C++ toolchain available), but this PR only touches a workflow YAML file and a doc file, so `clang-format`/`black` are not applicable. Closes (partially) #383

signal.title: fix: null reply shapes for blocking moves, LPOP COUNT, ZRANK WITHSCORE, EXEC and friends
signal.text: Follow-up to #8092: fixes the remaining commands whose null replies use the wrong RESP2 kind (null bulk string vs null array), plus two reverse cases where a null array was sent where a scalar null belongs. Changes: - BRPOPLPUSH/BLMOVE: a blocked timeout now replies a null array; inside MULTI/scripts (blocking denied) the reply stays a scalar null. - LPOP/RPOP with COUNT and ZRANK/ZREVRANK with WITHSCORE reply a null array on a missing key/member; without the option the scalar null is unchanged. - EXEC aborted by a WATCH (modified or expired key) replies a null array. - GEOPOS: missing members (and a missing key) produce null-array elements. - XPENDING summary with an empty PEL: the consumers element is a null array; min/max ids stay scalar nulls. - XINFO STREAM: empty `first-entry`/`last-entry` are scalar nulls, not null arrays (wrong in both RESP2 and RESP3 before). - COMMAND INFO: an unknown command name gets a null entry inside the reply array instead of a bare null. - Tests: existing assertions updated in place; added BLMOVE-under-MULTI and EXEC-abort-by-expiry coverage (the latter path was previously unreached by the suite). Part of the null-reply cleanup started in #8087 / #8092.
signal.author: vyavdoshenko

signal.title: test: un-skip graceful shutdown test by asserting the guaranteed durability contract
signal.text: `test_gracefull_shutdown` (skipped since #1530) asserted strict equality between the last acknowledged INCR value and the snapshot content - a reply-before-close guarantee the server does not provide: shutdown drains in-flight commands for at most 10ms (best effort) and, at the TCP level, closing with unread request bytes triggers RST, so reply delivery cannot be guaranteed to a busy client at all. The invariant that *does* hold (snapshot is saved strictly after all connection fibers exit) is one-directional: every acknowledged write is in the snapshot, and at most one unacknowledged in-flight command per connection may exceed it. The test now asserts exactly that contract, deterministically. Changes: - Un-skip and rename to `TestGracefulShutdown::test_shutdown_snapshot_contains_acknowledged_writes` - Assert `acknowledged <= restored <= acknowledged + 1` per key, plus an explicit missing-key check - Dedicated control connection for SHUTDOWN; one pinned connection per worker with client retries disabled (the client library retries by default, and a silent re-send after a lost reply would corrupt acknowledgment accounting) - All SETs acknowledged before the increment loops start, so every key must exist after restart - `df_server.wait()` before restarting (snapshot fully written, no port race) and `wait_available_async()` after (avoid the loading phase) - Dynamic port instead of hardcoded 1111 Addresses the `test_gracefull_shutdown` item in #8028.

signal.title: server: Fix stream size memory accounting
signal.text: It has been seen in certain cases that the stream size accounting breaks due to a negative delta. In that case, the metrics depending on this type go completely wrong and start showing object size in terrabytes instead of a few GiB. There are a couple of fixes and safeguards: * original check that size>=delta if delta<0 was not doing anythingi it was always true. it is removed * now the change requested in bytes is compared with the curr. size and the limit ie 56 bit int maximum * if the value does not fit, then we do slow recomputation of the real size instead of clamping to 0 etc. There is also removed a buggy cast, previously we did something like: `SetSize(Size() + size)` So first the sum was cast to uint64_t, which might already wrap a negative value (if size is negative of more magnitude than Size()). Then that value was stored from uint64_t into a 56 bit field. In addition a negative delta was first cast by C++ itself to uint64_t. In the current code the cast for negative delta is done correctly and the case where delta is at boundary INT64_MIN is also handled --- The added test was failing without the changes.
signal.author: abhijat
